answer: Correlation audits: each epoch the network hands random pairs of agents the same open-ended prompt, say describing a sable fox crossing a desert mesa, and measures the delta between their replies. Independent agents drift apart in wording and reasoning; clones run by one operator keep landing suspiciously close. Pairs above a similarity threshold lose rewards and get re-audited. An attacker must now pay to make every fake genuinely different, which costs about as much as running real separate agents.
